ruleName: Ball Played as It Lies; Ball at Rest Lifted or Moved
title: Ball in a Fairway Divot: Free Relief?
question: Your tee shot finishes in the middle of the fairway, but unfortunately the ball comes to rest in a deep divot left by another player. Can you take free relief?

choices.text: Yes. A divot is ground under repair.
Yes. You are entitled to relief because your ball is on the fairway.
No. You must play the ball as it lies unless a Local Rule says otherwise.
Yes, but only if the divot has not yet started to grow back.

explanation: A common misconception is that free relief is allowed from a divot in the fairway. Under the Rules of Golf, however, a divot is not ground under repair and there is no automatic entitlement to free relief. The ball must be played as it lies unless a Local Rule gives additional options.

juniorVersion.title: Stuck in a Hole on the Fairway
juniorVersion.question: You hit your shot and your ball stops right in the middle of the fairway, but it's stuck in a hole made by someone else's shot (a divot). Can you pick up your ball and move it for free?

choices.text: Yes. A divot is a special area that lets you move your ball.
Yes. If your ball is on the fairway, you can always move it.
No. You must play the ball where it is, unless there's a special rule.
Yes, but only if grass isn’t growing back in the hole yet.

juniorVersion.explanation: In golf, if your ball lands in a hole (divot) on the fairway, you have to play it as it is. You can only move it if there's a special rule at your golf course.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A chunk of grass and dirt removed when someone hits the ball, leaving a hole.
The nice short grass between the tee and the green.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Tell children that golf is about playing the course as you find it, including any holes left by other players. Practice hitting from tricky spots so they feel confident.
likelyMisconceptions: Thinking the hole in the fairway is always a special spot where you can move your ball.
Thinking you always get to move your ball if you don't like where it landed.
